coverage.text_review: Exhaustive over both lessons: titles, prose, visual/code panel text and annotations, wrap-ups, next-tile previews, and all remediation blocks. Nested visual panels included.
coverage.method: Compared learner-facing content with each concept's glossary blocked_future_concepts and required facts. Same-tile concepts were assessed in instructional order; wrap-ups may use concepts already taught. No deterministic gates were rerun and no generator reasoning or prior evaluator claims were used.

findings.rationale: Dataset snapshot retention, repair followed by revalidation, waitFor, fatal exits and configured-trigger inspection are explicitly part of the current dataset-gate facts, not leakage from recovery or artifact-dependency lessons. Behavior-test panels use release_gate only as an opaque dependent stage; they require no release eligibility calculations. Release eligibility and expected error cost are taught before their use. Promotion is a downstream action, not a requirement to understand later staged authorization.

Artifact identity checks remain within the dependency concept. Registry/run links, approved identities, secret references and promotion records are explicitly required staged-promotion facts, not premature lineage auditing. Reconciled uploads and repeated-recovery invariants are explicitly required recovery facts; they do not demand understanding later retraining-run idempotency. Full lineage verification occurs only in the lineage segment. The production-distribution preview is a passing next-tile mention.
